description: The bar chart illustrates five different layer grouping patterns—labeled Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, Spindle, and Bottleneck—used in the context of parameter-efficient fine-tuning design spaces. Each pattern is represented by a series of bars corresponding to four groups (G₁, G₂, G₃, G₄), with the horizontal axis indicating the group index and the vertical axis representing the number of layers in each group. The "Increasing" pattern shows a progressive rise in the number of layers from G₁ to G₄, with the tallest bar at G₄. The "Uniform" pattern displays equal bar heights across all four groups, indicating an even distribution of layers. The "Decreasing" pattern exhibits a downward trend, with the highest number of layers in G₁ and the lowest in G₄. The "Spindle" pattern features a peak in the middle, with higher bars at G₂ and G₃ and lower values at G₁ and G₄. Lastly, the "Bottleneck" pattern shows a dip in the middle, with taller bars at G₁ and G₄ and shorter bars at G₂ and G₃. All bars are rendered in a light green color, and the patterns are arranged side by side for direct comparison.
